import Mathlib

noncomputable abbrev putnam_2024_b1_solution : Set (ℕ × ℕ) := ({(2*l+1, l+1) | (l : ℕ)})
--{(2*l+1, l+1) | (l : ℕ)}
/--
Let $n$ and $k$ be positive integers. The square in the $i$th row and
$j$th column of an $n$-by-$n$ grid contains the number $i + j - k$.
For which $n$ and $k$ is it possible to select $n$ squares from the
grid, no two in the same row or column, such that the numbers
contained in the selected squares are exactly $1, ..., n$?
-/
theorem putnam_2024_b1
    (grid : (n : ℕ) → ℕ → Fin n → Fin n → ℤ)
    (grid_def : ∀ n k i j, grid n k i j = i.succ + j.succ - k)
    (valid : ℕ → ℕ → Prop)
    (valid_def : ∀ n k, valid n k ↔ 0 < n ∧ 0 < k ∧
      ∃ (f : Fin n → Fin n), f.Injective ∧
        Set.range (fun i => grid n k i (f i)) = Set.Ico (1 : ℤ) n) :
    { (n, k) | valid n k } = putnam_2024_b1_solution :=
  sorry

probe.proof:
by
  let g : (n : ℕ) → ℕ → Fin n → Fin n → ℤ := fun _ k i j => (i.succ : ℤ) + j.succ - k
  let v : ℕ → ℕ → Prop := fun n k => 0 < n ∧ 0 < k ∧ ∃ f : Fin n → Fin n, f.Injective ∧ Set.range (fun i => g n k i (f i)) = Set.Icc (1 : ℤ) n
  refine ⟨g, v, ?_⟩
  intro he
  have hl := he.mpr (by constructor <;> intros <;> rfl)
  have hv : v 1 1 := by
    dsimp [v]
    refine ⟨by decide, by decide, id, Function.injective_id, ?_⟩
    ext x
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩
      have hi : i = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
      subst i
      norm_num [g, Set.mem_Icc]
    · intro hx
      change (1 : ℤ) ≤ x ∧ x ≤ 1 at hx
      have hx' : x = 1 := le_antisymm hx.2 hx.1
      subst x
      exact ⟨0, by norm_num [g]⟩
  obtain ⟨_, _, f, _, hf⟩ := (hl.2 1 1).mp hv
  have hm : g 1 1 0 (f 0) ∈ Set.Ico (1 : ℤ) (1 : ℕ) := by
    rw [← hf]
    exact Set.mem_range_self 0
  norm_num at hm
